title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 54
paragraphs: During that day they made preparations to cross over; and on the next day they waited for the sun, wishing to see him rise, and meanwhile they burned every kind of incense upon the bridges and strewed the way with branches of myrtle. As the sun was rising, Xerxes poured a libation from a golden cup into the sea and prayed to the Sun that no accident might befall him such as would make him stop subduing Europe before he had come to its furthest limits. After praying, he threw the cup into the Hellespont, and with it a golden mixing-bowl and a Persian sword, which they call an akinakes. Whether he cast these into the sea as an offering dedicated to the Sun, or whether he had repented of having lashed the Hellespont and wished to make amends by a gift, I cannot say for certain.
